portName: Port of Key West (Pier B, Mallory Square)
seoTitle: Key West cruise port guide: Pier B, Duval, Hemingway
seoDescription: Key West ships dock at Pier B, a short walk from Duval Street. Hemingway Home $19 (2026), Fort Zachary Taylor $2.50 on foot. One ship a day. Back 60 min early.
quickAnswer: Key West is a docking port: almost every ship ties up at Pier B, in front of the Westin, a short walk from Mallory Square and the top of Duval Street. You need no transport for Old Town; the Hemingway Home is about a 20-minute walk. Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard.
intro: Key West is one of the easiest calls on a Caribbean itinerary. The ship docks beside Old Town, the island is flat, and the main sights are within walking distance. Since the 2020 referendum the city has kept a one-ship-a-day policy, so the town is rarely swamped by several ships at once. The real constraints are heat, afternoon storms in summer and early autumn, and the temptation to linger on Duval Street. The famous Mallory Square sunset may come after your ship has sailed.

terminals.name: Pier B
terminals.notes: Privately operated pier in the marina in front of the Westin. Used by nearly all cruise ships; under the city's one-ship policy it is the only berth for most calls. A short walk to Mallory Square and Duval Street.

terminals.name: Mallory Square Dock
terminals.notes: City-owned dock at Mallory Square, a few steps from Old Town. Used mainly by small ships, such as American Cruise Lines.

terminals.name: Outer Mole Pier (Navy)
terminals.notes: Navy-owned pier reached through the base, with a short shuttle into town. Not used by cruise ships under the city's one-ship policy; the Navy told the city in 2026 that it would end the lease, and future use is undecided.

walkability.detail: From Pier B or Mallory Square, Old Town and the north end of Duval Street are a short, flat walk. The Hemingway Home is about 20 minutes on foot. Shade is patchy; carry water in summer.

transportSections.time: Short walk to Mallory Square and Duval Street; about 20 min to the Hemingway Home
transportSections.detail: Old Town is compact and flat. Most visitors walk everywhere.

transportSections.cost: $2 per ride, paid in the app (2026)
transportSections.time: Book in the app; runs about 06:00–20:00
transportSections.detail: Replaced the Duval Loop bus from 2 January 2026. Download the free Key West Rides app, book a pick-up within Key West or Stock Island, and track the vehicle. Former Duval Loop stops are still served. Wheelchair users select the wheelchair icon when booking.

transportSections.time: About 5 min to the Hemingway Home
transportSections.detail: A taxi line waits just outside the port. Useful for Fort Zachary Taylor, Smathers Beach or Higgs Beach in heat or rain.

transportSections.mode: Old Town Trolley or Conch Tour Train
transportSections.detail: Sightseeing tours rather than transport. The trolley is hop-on, hop-off.

transportSections.time: A few minutes to anywhere on the island
transportSections.detail: Bikes suit the flat island. Scooters share narrow streets with cars, trolleys and golf carts; rent one only if you are confident riding.

returnTiming.rule: Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard (16:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard).
returnTiming.detail: Pier B is a short walk from Duval Street, so leave Old Town about 80 minutes before all-aboard. Leave earlier from the Hemingway Home, Fort Zachary Taylor or the beaches. Allow extra time if a storm comes through.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi from anywhere on the island; Key West is small and taxis, Uber and Lyft are widely available. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: $19 adult at the gate (2026), about 20 min walk

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner

excursionAdvice: For Old Town, the Hemingway Home and Fort Zachary Taylor you do not need a ship's tour: everything is walkable and tickets are sold at the gate. A ship's trip earns its price for snorkelling or diving on the reef or the Vandenberg wreck, where the boat operator has to fit your return time, and for anyone who cannot walk far in heat. The narrated trolley or Conch Tour Train can be bought locally.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at Pier B at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30.

steps.what: Walk off Pier B to Mallory Square and the north end of Duval Street before the heat builds.
Walk to the Hemingway Home (about 20 minutes) and take the 20–30-minute guided tour.
Walk or ride to the Southernmost Point for the photo.
Fort Zachary Taylor: $2.50 on foot. See the fort, then cool off by the water.
Lunch, for example at Blue Heaven.
Duval Street and Sloppy Joe's, or a narrated trolley loop.
Start back towards Pier B from Duval Street.

sights.name: Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum
sights.why: The writer's house and garden, with guided tours and the famous six-toed cats.
sights.cost: $19 adult, $7 child 6–12, under-6s free (2026); 3% fee on card and mobile payments
sights.tip: Open daily 09:00–17:00. Tours every 15 minutes from 09:15; tickets at the main gate only, no reservations.

sights.name: Fort Zachary Taylor Historic State Park
sights.why: A historic fort inside a state park within easy reach of Old Town, with space to cool off by the water.
sights.cost: $2.50 per pedestrian or cyclist, including the Monroe County surcharge (2026)
sights.tip: Park open 08:00 to sundown; the fort itself closes at 17:00.

sights.name: Mallory Square
sights.why: The waterfront square beside the cruise piers, famous for its sunset gathering with street performers.
sights.tip: Check whether sunset falls before your all-aboard; stay only if it does.

sights.name: Duval Street
sights.why: Old Town's main street of bars, live music and shops; Mallory Square is at its north end.
sights.tip: Walk it early, then use side streets for shade and the conch cottages.

sights.name: Southernmost Point
sights.why: One of the island's best-known photo stops.
sights.tip: Use a taxi or Key West Rides if the heat makes the walk hard.

sights.name: Old Town Trolley or Conch Tour Train
sights.why: Narrated loops of Old Town for anyone who prefers not to walk in the heat.
sights.tip: The trolley is hop-on, hop-off, so you can use it as transport between sights.

beaches.name: Fort Zachary Taylor State Park
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk, bike or taxi from Pier B
beaches.note: Combine with a visit to the fort.

beaches.name: Higgs Beach
beaches.howToGetThere: Taxi, bike or Key West Rides
beaches.time: A short ride across the island
beaches.note: A public beach outside Old Town.

beaches.name: Smathers Beach
beaches.note: A public beach outside Old Town; take a ride rather than walking in the heat.

food.dish: Conch fritters, Cuban sandwiches and key lime pie
food.where: Food vendors and waterfront restaurants around Mallory Square

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning to watch the Mallory Square sunset.
commonMistakes.fix: Check your all-aboard time first. Many ships sail before sunset.

commonMistakes.mistake: Waiting for the Duval Loop bus.
commonMistakes.fix: It was suspended in January 2026. Walk, or book the Key West Rides on-demand bus in its app.

commonMistakes.mistake: Walking to the beaches at midday in summer.
commonMistakes.fix: Take a taxi or ride for Smathers and Higgs, and carry water.

commonMistakes.mistake: Renting a scooter with no riding experience.
commonMistakes.fix: Streets are narrow and busy with cars, trolleys and golf carts. Walk or rent a bike.

commonMistakes.mistake: Staying on Duval Street until the last minute.
commonMistakes.fix: Leave Old Town 80 minutes before all-aboard; Pier B is close, but heat and storms slow you down.

safety: Key West is a low-risk port for visitors. The main hazards are heat and sun, summer thunderstorms, and traffic on narrow streets shared with scooters, bikes and golf carts. October and November still fall in hurricane season, so watch the forecast; ships may change itinerary. Duval Street is busy with bars, so keep an eye on belongings in crowds and drink sensibly in the heat.
accessibility: All three piers are described as wheelchair-friendly, and Old Town is flat. The Key West Rides on-demand buses are ADA accessible; choose the wheelchair option when booking. Ask at the Hemingway Home gate about access before buying a ticket.
rainyDay: Shelter in the Hemingway Home, the bars and shops of Duval Street, or take the covered trolley tour. Use a taxi or Key West Rides rather than waiting in the rain.
crowdTips: The city keeps a one-ship-a-day policy, so you rarely share the town with several ships' passengers at once. Go to the Hemingway Home and the Southernmost Point early, when queues are shortest, and leave Duval Street for the afternoon.

faqs.q: Where do cruise ships dock in Key West?
faqs.a: Almost always at Pier B, in front of the Westin. Small ships may use the Mallory Square dock. The Navy's Outer Mole is not used under the city's one-ship policy.

faqs.q: Is Key West walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. Mallory Square and Duval Street are a short walk from Pier B; the Hemingway Home is about 20 minutes on foot.

faqs.q: Is Key West a tender port?
How many cruise ships can visit Key West a day?
faqs.a: The city keeps a one-ship-per-day policy based on the 2020 referendum, with ships using the privately owned Pier B.

faqs.q: Is the Duval Loop bus still running?
faqs.a: No. It was suspended on 2 January 2026 and replaced by the Key West Rides on-demand service at $2 a ride, booked in the app.

faqs.q: How much is the Hemingway Home?
faqs.a: $19 for adults and $7 for children aged 6–12 in 2026, with a 3% fee on card payments. Open daily 09:00–17:00.

faqs.q: Beaches near Key West cruise port?
faqs.a: Fort Zachary Taylor State Park is closest ($2.50 on foot). Higgs and Smathers beaches are a short taxi ride.

faqs.q: What can I do in Key West in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Hemingway Home, the Southernmost Point, Fort Zachary Taylor and Duval Street, all on foot or with a short ride.
